Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

tidypptsdm 1.1.0

  • plot_monitor(type = "intake") draws stacked bars as fid_monitor() of pptsdm did: the share of each pig in the station’s feed intake (top) and its feed intake in kg (bottom), with the daily total above the bar. One colour per pig in both panels and one legend; the number of colours grows with the number of pigs. Pigs without visit or with low feed intake on the last day are marked in the legend. The heat map of 1.0.0 is now type = "heatmap" and is no longer in the HTML report.
  • plot_monitor(type = "trend") has a body weight panel: the mean of the pigs’ daily median weight, with a band from the lightest to the heaviest pig.

tidypptsdm 1.0.0

The package is renamed from pptsdm to tidypptsdm and rewritten on top of tidypptsda. None of the old functions remain; see the article “从 pptsdm 迁移” for the mapping.

New design

  • Data are read with read_station() and prepared with prep_visits() from tidypptsda (both re-exported): the same columns and units for NEDAP and FIRE (feed intake in g, body weight in kg, duration in seconds), unidentified visits kept with identified = FALSE, pigs moved to another station resolved. Every function accepts a folder of exports, a raw export in R, or the result of either function, and never modifies its input.
  • run_monitor() computes everything once: monitor_stations(), monitor_houses(), monitor_pigs(), monitor_hours() and the alerts of the last day (station_down, unidentified, feed_drop, pig_no_visit, pig_low_feed). Thresholds are arguments (low_feed_kg, max_unidentified_pct, max_feed_drop_pct, iqr_k).
  • The daily tables are long, with one row per unit and day, also for days without any visit; wide_table() gives the wide view.
  • plot_monitor() draws one plot per station: "trend", "intake" (heat map of feed intake per pig and day), "weight" and "hours"; save_monitor_plots() saves them.
  • write_monitor_report() writes an offline HTML report to browse station by station, in the style of tidypptsda::write_report(). It replaces fid_monitor() (PDF) and station_monitor() (PNG files).
  • write_monitor_tables() writes an Excel workbook with colour scales, or CSV files. It replaces table_monitor().
  • schedule_monitor() writes the daily script and registers it in the Windows Task Scheduler, or prints the crontab line on Linux and macOS. It replaces monitor_schedule() and monitor_all().
  • Messages with cli and verbose = 0/1/2, as in tidypptsda.
  • Dependencies: cli, data.table, ggplot2 and tidypptsda. cowplot, lubridate, patchwork, pptsda, purrr, scales and tidyr are no longer needed; openxlsx and taskscheduleR are optional.
  • The logo and favicons of pptsdm are kept.
  • Examples use the nedap and fire datasets of tidypptsda and run everywhere; the package has tests.

Fixed problems of pptsdm 0.1.4

  • The monitoring window had days + 1 days, and some tables ended the day before the others. Now every table covers the same days days ending on end_date.
  • Pigs without any visit on a day were missing from the low feed intake table; they are now "no_visit" and give an alert.
  • Durations were divided by 60 in one table and by 3600 in another; NEDAP durations are seconds and every column now says its unit (occupation_h, occupation_min).
  • The colour scales of the Excel sheets covered one column too many, and the feed_time_n sheet had none.
  • station_monitor() gave every PNG the size of the first station, and its date axis showed only the month.
  • fid_monitor() failed with more pigs at a station than colours.
  • hour_stat(), fid_monitor() and station_monitor() modified the data passed to them.
  • monitor_schedule() only worked on Windows with a C:/Temp folder.
